## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

 Urging them to exercise caution where distrust is warranted, the Buddha compared the growth of defilements around a person to banyans and parasitic plants overtaking a tree; he then recounted a tale of the past wherein a tree-spirit dwelling in the upper canopy of a silk-cotton tree (*koṭasimbali*) became terrified after seeing a bird excrete ingested banyan seeds into the branches, dreading the eventual destruction of her dwelling.
